images.title: The point hops left
images.purpose: Show the decimal point moving one place left for each zero in the divisor while the digits stay in their columns.
images.composition: Four rows of the same digits stacked in the centre with the digits lined up in fixed columns; the decimal point is the only thing that moves; the divisor is written at the right of each row and one short rule line sits at the bottom.
exact_structure: Five fixed digit columns, numbered 1 to 5 from the left; the digits 1, 8 and 7 are teal #0072B2 and sit in columns 3, 4 and 5 in every row.
Row 1: 18.7, digits in columns 3, 4, 5, the point between column 4 and column 5; no divisor label.
Row 2: 1.87, the point between column 3 and column 4; at the right the label ÷ 10.
Row 3: 0.187, a grey #6B7280 0 in column 2 and the point between column 2 and column 3; at the right ÷ 100.
Row 4: 0.0187, grey #6B7280 zeroes in columns 1 and 2 and the point between column 1 and column 2; at the right ÷ 1000.
Every decimal point is a large reddish purple #CC79A7 dot; a small reddish purple curved arrow between each pair of rows shows the point hopping one place left (3 arrows).
Bottom line: Move the point one place left for each zero
labels: Move the point one place left for each zero
rejection: digits 1, 8, 7 shifting columns between rows instead of staying lined up
more or fewer than 3 hop arrows
images.takeaway: Dividing by 10, 100 or 1000 moves the decimal point left by as many places as the divisor has zeroes.
images.description: Four rows, 18.7, 1.87, 0.187 and 0.0187, with the digits 1, 8, 7 lined up and a purple decimal point hopping one place left for each ÷ 10, ÷ 100 and ÷ 1000.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video stating the rule for dividing by 10, 100, 1000 and 10000.
images.teaching_notes: Students should watch only the purple point and count how many places it moves for each divisor.

image_decisions.why: The rule is a movement of the point, which a stacked row picture shows directly.
